question: A child is born to an HBsAg-positive mother. On examination, the child looks normal and there is no yellowish discoloration of the skin. How will you manage the further immunization of this child?

answers.option: Give him Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) 1 mL intramuscular, hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 1, and 6 months
Give him the usual hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 1, and 6 months
No Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) or hepatitis B vaccine needed
Give him Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) 0.5 mL intramuscular, hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 1, and 6 months
Only give him Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) 2 ml intramuscular

question: An 11-year-old girl presented to the clinic with complaints of difficulty walking and bilateral symmetrical lower limb weakness. Past medical history revealed a recent gastrointestinal upset. On examination, power was reduced in both limbs and the deep tendon reflexes were absent. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed an increase in total protein concentration without pleocytosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl presents to the outpatient department with complaints of spontaneous bruising and petechiae all over the body. There is no history of hemarthrosis, mucosal bleeding, drug intake, or trauma. Past medical history reveals a recent episode of sore throat. Laboratory investigations show a prolonged bleeding time and a platelet count of 40,000/mm3. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman known case of diabetes mellitus has just delivered a baby at the 37th week of gestation by a cesarean section. The baby cried immediately after birth but after an hour he develops sudden onset tachypnea with a rate of 66 breaths/min, nasal flaring, chest recessions, and expiratory grunt. What is the most likely diagnosis and what x-ray findings will accompany the respective diagnosis?

answers.option: Transient tachypnea of the newborn, streaky shadowing radiating out from the hila
Pneumothorax, air in the upper parts
Respiratory distress syndrome, ground glass appearance of the lung field with generalized atelectasis
Pneumothorax, air in the lower parts
Meconium aspiration syndrome, hilar shadows with streaky shadows and patchy atelectasis

question: Parents bring their 8-month-old child to the clinic with the concern that their child does not look normal as compared to other kids his age. On examination, the child has coarse facial features with a wide nasal bridge, flattened midface, and a large forehead. There is also hepatosplenomegaly. Radiographic evidence shows the beaked appearance of the anteroinferior surface of the vertebrae, oar-shaped ribs, and irregular hyperostotic diaphysis and metaphysics. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A mother brings her 2-month-old child with concerns about ambiguous genitalia. On examination, the testis is impalpable. Which of the following investigations will help confirm the sex of the child?

A 10-year-old unimmunized child weighing 30 Kg, belonging to a poor socio-economic group, and a resident of urban slums presents to the outpatient department with complaints of high-grade continuous fever for 10 days. On examination, the patient has a toxic look, his tongue is coated, and the spleen is palpable 3 cm below the costal margin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old female comes to the outpatient department with a history of deterioration of school performance and abnormal jerky movements for the last two months. On examination, there is dystonia and Kayser-Fleischer rings in the eyes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a side-effect of ethambutol?

A mother brings her 2-year-old child with the concern of his slowing growth over the past year. After a thorough history, examination, and relevant investigations it is found that the bone age (BA) is equal to height age (HT) but is less than the constitutional age (CA). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A mother brings her 1-year-old child with the concern that she feels like her child's head is larger than his age. His frontal occipital circumference (FOC) is 49 cm. Which of the following is the normal value of FOC at this age?

A 2-year-old fully immunized, and healthy child comes to the clinic with complaints of crusted lesions on the face and trunk. There is no history of associated fever. On examination, the child is afebrile and the lesions are medium to large. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with complaints of blood and mucus in his stools for the past 9 days. He also gives a history of low-grade fever and mild abdominal pain. Which of the following is responsible for this presentation?

A 10-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of blood and mucus in stool associated with high-grade fever and crampy abdominal pain. On examination, the body temperature is 104°F (40°C). Which of the following is the most likely cause of this presentation?
Which of the following tools is not used in the assessment of a child with behavioral disturbances?

answers.option: Interview with the parents and child
Specific tests of memory, language, and motor skills

question: An infant born at 38 weeks of gestation starts jittering soon after birth. Which of the following levels should be checked first to further manage the child?

An infant was born at 38 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 4.5 Kg. Soon after birth, the infant had jitters, and on further evaluation, his blood glucose was found to be 37 mg/dL. Which of the following could be the most probable cause of this clinical picture?

A 5-month-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of alopecia and vesicular eruptions around different body areas. Which of the following mineral deficiencies could cause this clinical presentation?

A 1-year-old baby weighing 5 Kg presents to the clinic with complaints of lethargy and drowsiness. On further evaluation the child was hypoglycemic. How much 10% glucose will be given through the intravenous route to resolve the symptoms?

A 1-year-old male child presents to the clinic with the complaint of diarrhea and flecks of blood and mucus in stool. The child is not breastfed and drinks cow milk instead. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
A 3-month-old child is exclusively on cow milk. Which of the following nutritional deficiency is he at risk of as compared to a child who is exclusively breastfed?

A 2-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of barking cough and hoarseness. Acute laryngotracheobronchitis is suspected. Which of the following X-ray is advised to confirm the diagnosis?

answers.option: X-ray of the neck, X-ray of the neck
X-ray of the chest, lateral view
X-ray of the neck, antero-posterior view
X-ray of the neck, postero-anterior view
X-ray of the neck, lateral view

question: A 7-year-old child presents to the clinic with the complaint of prominent papillae on the whole surface of the tongue giving it the appearance of a strawberry tongue. The patient also complains of high-grade fever with chills.  Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child presents to the emergency department with sudden onset difficulty breathing and urticaria after eating a pack of peanuts. Which of the following will be used in the next step of management of the child?

A 16-year-old girl presents to the clinic with a complaint of primary amenorrhea, a webbed neck, and short stature. The mother also gives a history of edema around the feet in the newborn period. Laboratory investigations show raised FSH and LH. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-month-old infant presents to the clinic with complaints of discharge from the umbilicus. On examination, the umbilical area is red and inflamed and there is a purulent discharge oozing from the umbilicus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following X-ray views is used to see respiratory manifestations of pertussis?
Which of the following cells are seen in a bone marrow biopsy sample of a patient with Gaucher's disease?

A 4-month-old infant presents to the outpatient department with complaints of failure to thrive and yellow-brown discoloration of the skin. On examination, there is hepatosplenomegaly and cherry-red spots on the macula. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child presents to the emergency department with complaints of high-grade fever, sore throat, and difficulty breathing. On examination, the temperature is 102°F (38.89 °C), drooling of saliva from the mouth, tachypnea, and flaring of alae nasi. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the recommended dose of vitamin A in an infant less than 6 months of age diagnosed with measles?

A 7-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of lethargy and generalized swelling of the body. The boy mentions that his urine has a frothy appearance as of late. On examination, he has bilateral pitting edema. A 24-hour urine analysis shows proteinuria of 3.85 g/day. How will you manage this child?

A 10-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of muscle weakness and a violaceous rash around the upper eyelid. On examination, the Gower sign is positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most specific confirmatory test for the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus?

An 8-year-old child presents to the emergency department with the complaint of inability to walk for 2 days. The child also informs that he has not passed urine since last night. On examination, the power is decreased in both lower limbs. There is also a loss of sensations at the level of L-2. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old child presents to the emergency department with a history of fever for 5 days, fits, and loss of consciousness. On examination, his GCS is 6/15, with signs of meningeal irritation, and a rash present on the legs and buttocks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
